title: Rating-step column contract declares produced output for tables with no factors/entries (runtime skips them)
description: _rating_step_columns adds a table's outputColumn to `produced` for any table with a non-empty outputColumn (l.794-797: `out = t.get("outputColumn", ""); if out: produced.add(out)`), ignoring whether the table has usable `factors`/`entries`. The runtime _apply_rating_table returns the frame unchanged (no column produced) when factors or entries are empty: `if not factors or not entries or not output_col: return lf`. So a rating table with outputColumn set but empty entries (an in-progress config) is declared produced by the contract but never materialised. As with banding, projection.py:2321 subtracts the over-declared `produced` from upstream demand, so a downstream consumer of that outputColumn gets it pruned away yet the runtime never creates it -> column-not-found at materialisation in projected profiles. The contract should mirror the executor's factors/entries guard before declaring a table output as produced.
evidence: _rating_step_columns l.794-797 declares produced from outputColumn presence only; _apply_rating_table (_rating.py l.517) skips tables with empty factors or entries; demand subtraction at projection.py l.2321 applies (RATING_STEP concrete contract via columns=_rating_step_columns at l.807). normalise_rating_tables (_rating_step_config.py l.304) does not drop such tables.
